record.paper_title: KAM theorems and open problems for infinite dimensional Hamiltonian with short range
record.original_question: Consider an infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian on the lattice Z^d with action-angle variables (I_j, phi_j) and symplectic structure sum_j dI_j wedge dphi_j, of the form H = sum_{j in Z^d} omega_j I_j + epsilon sum_{<i,j>} f_{<i,j>}(I_i, I_j; phi_i, phi_j), where the perturbation f is short range. In known KAM results for this setting, invariant tori are obtained near strongly localized action profiles such as I_j^0 = exp(-|j|^{d+alpha}), and later work suggested weaker subexponential restrictions. Does an infinite-dimensional KAM torus exist when the initial action profile has only polynomial decay, namely epsilon_j = I_j^0 approximately |j|^{-M} for some sufficiently large M > 0?

evidence.quote: In 1986, Frohlich, Spencer and Wayne[9] generalized Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) theorem to infinite dimensional Hamiltonian H = sum_{j in Z^d} omega_j I_j + epsilon sum_{<i,j>} f_{i,j}(I_i,I_j;phi_i,phi_j) with symplectic structure sum_j dI_j wedge dphi_j where f is of short range.

The initial conditions (1.17) implies that the action (or the amplitude) decays too fast such that the infinite dimensional KAM tori look like to be of finite dimension. Weaker restrictions were later suggested in Poschel[18]: epsilon_j = I_j^0 approximately exp(-(log|j|)^(1+alpha)) with some alpha > 0. Kuksin[15] and Bourgain[6] proposed the following open problem: Problem 1. Is there any infinite dimensional KAM tori for the initial conditions with polynomial decay epsilon_j = I_j^0 approximately |j|^{-M} with some large M > 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian system on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with action–angle coordinates $(I_j,\varphi_j)_{j\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ and symplectic form $\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}^d} dI_j\wedge d\varphi_j$. Let the Hamiltonian be
$$H = \sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\omega_j I_j \;+\; \varepsilon\sum_{\langle i,j\rangle} f_{\langle i,j\rangle}(I_i,I_j;\varphi_i,\varphi_j),$$
where $\omega = (\omega_j)_{j\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ is a frequency vector, the sum $\sum_{\langle i,j\rangle}$ runs over nearest-neighbour pairs (so the perturbation is short range), each $f_{\langle i,j\rangle}$ is real-analytic in its arguments and uniformly bounded, and $\varepsilon>0$ is a small parameter.

For a fixed initial action profile $I^0 = (I_j^0)_{j\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ with $I_j^0>0$, an "infinite-dimensional KAM torus with profile $I^0$" means an invariant torus of $H$ obtained as a small perturbation of the unperturbed torus $\{I_j = I_j^0,\ \varphi_j\in\mathbb{T}\}$ supporting a quasi-periodic flow with frequency vector close to $\omega$.

Existence of such tori is known under strong decay assumptions on the profile, e.g. $I_j^0 \asymp \exp(-|j|^{d+\alpha})$ for some $\alpha>0$, and under the weaker subexponential condition $I_j^0 \asymp \exp(-(\log|j|)^{1+\alpha})$.

Question: Does there exist a choice of frequencies $\omega$, of admissible nearest-neighbour interaction terms $f_{\langle i,j\rangle}$, and of $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that, for all $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$, the Hamiltonian $H$ admits an infinite-dimensional KAM torus whose initial action profile decays only polynomially, i.e. $I_j^0 \asymp |j|^{-M}$ for some sufficiently large $M>0$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question, attributed to Kuksin and Bourgain, of constructing infinite-dimensional KAM tori for short-range lattice Hamiltonians with only polynomially decaying initial action profile appears to remain open. Recent progress on full-dimensional tori for 1D NLS (Bourgain, Cong, and others) extends results to slower-than-exponential decay rates of the form $\exp(-(\log|n|)^\sigma)$, but no construction with purely polynomial decay $|j|^{-M}$ in the short-range lattice setting has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Towards sharp regularity: Full-dimensional tori in C^∞ vector fields over T^∞
status_evidence.snippet: Cong extended Bourgain's work on NLS, obtaining C^∞ full-dimensional tori whose radius satisfies a slower decay for any σ > 2: I_n ∼ e^{-ln^σ |n|} as |n|→∞.
status_evidence.claim: Best known decay for full-dimensional tori is still subexponential, not polynomial.

status_evidence.title: On the Kolmogorov theorem for some infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems of short range
status_evidence.snippet: Proof based on combination of Kolmogorov's idea and that of Fröhlich, Spencer, Wayne, and Pöschel.
status_evidence.claim: Recent KAM results for short-range lattice Hamiltonians still rely on strong (super-polynomial) decay assumptions.
